questions.q: Why does a classic red team engagement deliberately keep the blue team blind to when the attack will happen?
options: Because blue team members are not cleared to know engagement details
Because the blindness is what makes the test an honest measurement of real-world detection capability
Because the red team's contract legally requires secrecy from the client
Because blue team tools cannot be adjusted mid-engagement
questions.explain: If the SOC knows an attack is coming, every analyst is on high alert and the result says nothing about an ordinary day. The blindness is what makes the measurement honest.

questions.q: What is the blue team's actual role during a red team engagement?
options: To do their real job — watch the SIEM, investigate suspicious activity, and respond as if it's real
To shut down all systems the moment the engagement window opens
To write the final report on the red team's behalf
To disable logging so the red team isn't detected prematurely
questions.explain: The blue team's job during a red team engagement is simply their normal SOC function, performed without knowing whether any given alert is the test or a real incident.

questions.q: What makes purple teaming different from red team vs. blue team, according to this lesson?
options: Purple teaming uses entirely different tools than red or blue teaming
Purple teaming is a separate, permanent third team with its own dedicated staff
Purple teaming only happens after a breach has already occurred
Purple teaming is a deliberately collaborative mode where red and blue work together in real time on the same techniques
questions.explain: Purple team isn't a third roster of people — it's red and blue deliberately removing the fog of war and working side by side, technique by technique.

questions.q: In a purple team exercise, what happens immediately after red executes a technique that blue's SIEM fails to detect?
options: The finding is logged for the final report and revisited weeks later
The engagement is immediately terminated for safety reasons
Red and blue diagnose the gap together in the room and keep iterating until it's fixed
Blue is given the red team's full toolkit to use independently afterward
questions.explain: The defining feature of purple teaming is closing the gap in the same session — diagnosing why detection failed and fixing it before moving to the next technique.

questions.q: What trade-off does purple teaming make compared to a red team engagement, per this lesson?
options: It gives up the blind, true-to-life measurement in exchange for a much faster detection-engineering feedback loop
It gives up all use of the MITRE ATT&CK framework in exchange for simplicity
It gives up any involvement from the blue team in exchange for red team autonomy
It gives up measuring detection coverage entirely in exchange for a focus on exploitation depth
questions.explain: Purple teaming sacrifices the honest, blind measurement a red team engagement provides, but gets gaps fixed in minutes instead of waiting for a report weeks later.
